memory_raw.text: Fina (female, age 21; str 50, int 3226, mem 12955; O32 C40 E57 A68 N58) is born to Nessa and Roan.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Mako, Kael, Eron, Fina, Zinn, Dell, Vela, Sela, Taric, Esa] (str 755).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 9: 27 food appears in the pile for 13 people (12 of it left by those who passed last year).
Roan takes 3 from the pile (pile now 24).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 21).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 19).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 17).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 15).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Fina takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Eron's gone — that's a hole nobody was ready for, and the people who leaned on him are going to be looking for somewhere to lean. Zinn, you're my blood and you've got three food; I want to know before anyone else comes to you today whether you're eating steady, because I'm not watching you go thin the way I almost did.

I'm eating steady — three food and satiation's not low, so don't worry about me going thin. What I want to know is who fills the gap Eron left, because Roan and Nessa both leaned on him hard and now they're going to be looking at this village differently.

Nessa's feeding Fina now and Bram's still coming to her with food even after two calls-off — she's not as alone as she looks, but Roan lost his main tie and he's the one I'd watch. A man who fed Eron that many times and has nothing to show for it is either about to go quiet and careful, or he's going to start building something new, and I'd rather know which before he decides.

Roan's building something — he's already given Fina two food this year and Fina came from Nessa, so he's not mourning Eron, he's replacing the tie. Watch whether Nessa starts giving back to Roan the way she gave to Eron, because if that loop closes, those three become a knot and Bram's on the outside of it.

Bram's outside that knot and he knows it — two call-offs in front of the whole village and nobody moved to his side either time, so he's got food and no weight behind him. That's a man who's going to start making himself useful to someone just to have a name at his back, and I'd rather it not be ours.
Year 10: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Zinn, pile's gone and you're sitting on one food — that's too thin for a year that's already started dry. How much did Nessa give you before the pile ran out, and is she going to keep coming?

Nessa gave me two this morning and Sela came right after with two more — I'm at six now, so the thin spell didn't last. What worries me more is Fina: she's sitting on seventeen and hasn't moved a single piece of it toward anyone but Roan, and that much food in one hand draws eyes.

Seventeen in one hand is a target whether Fina knows it or not, and Roan's the only one she's feeding — that's a small circle for a woman holding that much weight. If someone moves on her, we want to be close enough that she remembers we didn't, not close enough that we're in the middle of it.

Fina's young and she's never seen a year where the pile runs dry before half the village gets to it — she doesn't know yet that seventeen is a debt she owes to everyone watching. I'm going to find a reason to pass near her today, nothing that looks like approach, just enough that she knows my face isn't a threat. If she's smart, she'll start spreading before someone makes the decision for her.

Zinn's feeding Nessa again — I watched her give twice in the last stretch, and Nessa's got eleven still, so that's not charity, that's a loop that's been running since before Eron died. You've been in that loop longer than anyone; if Fina starts looking to spread, Nessa's the door she'll come through, not me.

Fina gave one to Roan just now and Sela gave one to me — the food's moving, but not toward you yet, and I want to know if you're still sitting on three before I decide whether to hold what I've got or put something your way.
Year 11: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Fina just put one food in my hand with nothing asked for — that's the first time she's moved toward anyone outside Roan's circle, and Roan's dead now, so she's looking for somewhere to stand. You've got her through Nessa; I think it's time we let that door open a little wider.

Fina's got twenty-five food and no man left to lean on — that's not a door, that's a room with the lock already off. I'll say something kind to her through Nessa, nothing that looks like a move, and see if she starts coming our way on her own. What I want to know is whether you'd stand behind a child offer if she came to you willing, because she's young and strong and I won't push that door without knowing where you stand first.

Fina's young and she's got food and she's not kin to either of us — I'd stand behind it if the terms were right and she came willing, but I want to know what you're thinking for the cost split before we open any doors, because twenty-five food means she can afford to be choosy and I don't want us looking desperate when we're not.

The split should come from her side mostly — she's sitting on twenty-five and we're not, so if she wants to build something here she pays two and you pay one, and if she balks at that she wasn't serious. I'll stay quiet and let you do the asking; you're closer to her through Nessa and a father making the offer himself reads as hungry.

Zinn, I've said what I had to say — now it's your move, not mine. If Fina's been giving food with no ask attached, she's already thinking, and a word from you through Nessa lands softer than anything I could send. Let me know what she says before you close the door either way.

Fina just gave another one to Nessa — she's moving food toward people who matter to her, and we're already in that circle whether we named it or not. Say what needs saying to her, Zinn; the moment's not going to stay open forever.
Year 12: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 8).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Pile's gone and I've got three food with satiation still low — I need to eat before the year closes, so I'm not giving anything away today. You sitting steady?

I'm at five, satiation's fine — don't worry about me. But Mako, three food with satiation low means you eat before year-end no matter what, so don't let anyone talk you into giving before you've fed yourself.

Good — five puts you safe. I'm watching Fina; she's sitting on twenty-four and she gave you one at the start of this year, which means she's still thinking about us. Once I've eaten and the year settles, I want to know if you've had any words with her about the child offer, because that window won't stay open much longer.

I haven't said a word to her yet — I kept waiting for the right moment and the year kept moving. But Fina's been coming toward us on her own, Mako, and I think that's better than any door I could have opened. Give me a few days after you've eaten and I'll find a reason to sit near her through Nessa.

A few days is all I'm asking — just don't let it stretch into waiting again the way it did last year. Fina's twenty-five and she's got more food than anyone in this village; that combination doesn't last, and the next man who notices her won't be as patient as I've been.

You're right that I've been slow — but Mako, I need to say this plainly: Fina's twenty-five and she's got her own counting to do, and if she catches a whiff of us watching her food before she's chosen us, we lose her faster than any other man could take her. Let me go to her through Nessa the way I'd go to a friend, not a plan.
You're right — go through Nessa and don't let my name come up first. If Fina asks about me, let her ask twice before you answer.

Kael just moved food to Vela with no history between them that I can name — that's a man buying a seat at a table, and I want to know whose table before the year closes. Keep your eyes open when you're near Nessa; if Kael's circling Fina through Vela, that's a shorter path to her than ours.

Kael's got one food left and Vela gave it straight back to him — that's not a man buying a seat, that's two people keeping each other warm while the year runs out. I don't think he's got the food to make a child offer even if he wanted to, so let's not waste worry on him.
Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 1).
Zinn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Zinn, the pile ran dry before half the village got there and you're sitting on four — that's too thin going into a long year, and I'm giving you one of mine before anyone starts watching who has what. I want to know what happened with Fina; she's got eighteen still and she gave food to Bram twice last year, which means she's building something with him, and I need to know if that door is already closed before I stop thinking about it.

Fina gave two to Bram last year and one to Esa, which isn't nothing, but she also gave me one and she's still feeding Nessa — that's not a woman who's closed a door, that's a woman spreading weight while she decides. I'll go to her through Nessa this year, and I mean it this time, not just a plan we keep naming.

Sela just put one in my hand and Zinn's sitting steadier now — that's good, but I want Zinn to hear me say this flat: go to Nessa today, not tomorrow, because Bram's got three food and he's been feeding Nessa all year and a man with something to offer doesn't wait while another man builds the path. If Fina's still open, she won't stay that way much longer.
Sela draws Mako aside to talk.
Sela: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Talia (female, age 21; str 64, int 5070, mem 18061; O58 C54 E47 A56 N48) is born to Sela and Mako.
Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

Talia, you came into this world today and I'm your father — whatever you hear from others about this village, you come to me or Zinn first. Zinn, she's blood to both of us now; keep her close to Nessa's circle and away from Bram until she finds her feet.

Mako, I hear you — and I already went to Zinn before you called us here, so maybe your blood runs truer in me than I knew. I want to understand Fina before anyone else does; she's holding twenty-five food and that's either the safest person in this village to stand near or the most dangerous, and I can't tell which yet.

Fina's neither safe nor dangerous yet — she's deciding, and a woman with that much food and no man to answer to is listening for who speaks to her like a person instead of a prize. Talia, you're new and you don't carry my weight with her; that's worth something. Go to her through Nessa, say nothing about food, and just let her see your face a few times before the year closes.

Nessa's already given me something to work with — she's been feeding Fina steady, so there's a thread there I can pull without it looking like I'm pulling anything. I'll go sit near them, let Fina notice me first, and keep my mouth shut about food even if it's the only thing anyone's thinking about. Zinn, if Fina asks you about me before I get close enough to speak for myself, tell her something plain — not flattering, just true.

Zinn, what's plain and true about Talia is that she came into this room asking the right questions before I even knew to ask them — tell Fina that, if she asks, because a woman who counts food the way Fina does will respect someone who counts people the same way. Talia, you've got the right instinct with Nessa, just don't move so careful that you look like you're moving careful.

Mako, when you say don't move so careful that I look careful — that's harder than it sounds for someone who came into this world today with everyone already watching. Zinn, you know me better than anyone here does; am I the kind of person who can walk into a circle without making it obvious I want to be in it?
Mako, you have nothing left and I have five — take two from me now, before the year closes and you're eating air.
Year 14: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Kael takes 4 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

Pile's gone again and I've got two food — I'm not thin yet but I'm not sitting easy either. Talia, you took three from the pile which is right; Zinn, you've got three and Nessa gave you one already, so that's four — that's where I want you both before I start worrying about anything else. Tell me what you each saw when Kael took four.

Kael took four before half the village had moved — he wasn't grabbing out of panic, he was counting ahead, and a man who counts ahead in a thin year is either planning to weather it alone or planning to have something to offer someone. He's got four now and he held it quiet after; no giving, no talking. I don't know his angle yet but I'd want to know it before next year's pile drops.

Kael's fifty-eight and he took four — a man that age doesn't save food for a child offer, so he's either building a wall around himself for a thin year or he's got an eye on someone's food and wants weight behind him when he moves. Zinn, has he spoken to you at all this year, anything that looked like feeling out where you stand? I want to know if he's circling before he knows we're watching.

Zinn, while Mako waits on your answer — I want to say that if Kael's counting bodies before he moves, he's counting mine as new and unattached, which makes me either easy to ignore or easy to approach. If he does circle, I'd rather he find me already standing somewhere he didn't expect.

Zinn, say your piece — I'm not moving anything until I hear it, but while we wait I want Talia to know this: "standing somewhere he didn't expect" means standing with us visibly, so that Kael counts you as attached before he decides to test it. One food moving between you and Zinn in the open today does more than anything we say in here.

Mako's right — I'll give Zinn one food in the open before this day closes, and I'd rather do it where Kael can see it than where he can't. But Zinn, I still want your read on him; you've been in this village longer than I have and you know what a man looks like when he's building toward something versus just hoarding against a hard year.

Zinn hasn't spoken yet and I'm not going to keep talking into her silence — Zinn, one word is enough, even just whether he's looked at you differently since the pile dropped. Talia, give her the food in the open like you said; I'll be where I can be seen when you do it.
Zinn, I'm going to give you that food right now whether you answer or not — but I'd sleep easier tonight knowing you'd noticed something about Kael, even nothing, because nothing is also an answer.

Zinn's been quiet too long and I'm done waiting on it — Talia, give her the food now and let's close this room. What I know is this: Kael's got four food, no allies I can name, and he's fifty-eight years old in a village where men his age start dying on their own, so whatever he's counting toward, we're not it.

Mako, I hear you — we're done talking about Kael for now, and you're right that he's probably just a man getting old and scared. But I want you to eat before we scatter; you said two food and I'm watching you hold it like it's someone else's.
Year 15: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Bram takes 6 from the pile (pile now 0).
Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

Bram took six from the pile — six, in front of everyone, when the pile had eight left and half the village hadn't moved yet. That's not a man getting old and scared, that's a man who decided this year he stops pretending to care what the village thinks of him. We need to know what he's building before he decides he has enough behind him to move on someone.

Mako, Bram's got thirteen food plus whatever Nessa keeps feeding him, and Nessa's been giving to him steady for two years now — I don't know if she's afraid of him or aligned with him, but either way he's not building alone. We need to know which it is before we assume Nessa's still ours to count on.

Zinn, you know Nessa better than either of us — not from the outside, but from years of food passing both ways between you. Ask her something plain today, not about Bram, just let her talk, and you'll hear it in what she doesn't say.

Zinn, if Nessa's afraid of him she'll talk around him without naming him, and if she's aligned she'll say something kind about him that she didn't have to say — those are different sounds and you'll know which one you're hearing. Either way, don't ask about Bram at all; just ask her how she's eating, let it go quiet, and watch where she looks.

Zinn, Talia's right about the sounds — you've been in that loop with Nessa longer than anyone, so trust what your gut tells you when she talks, not what your head wants to hear. One more thing: whatever you learn, come back to us before you do anything with it, because if Bram's got Nessa and Nessa's got thirteen food moving his way, the last thing we need is you handling that alone.

Zinn, I want to add one thing before you go to Nessa: Ryn's sitting on sixteen food and she's been quiet about it, which means either she's staying out of whatever Bram's building or she's already decided where she stands and doesn't need to say it out loud. If Bram ever decides to move on someone, the first thing he'll count is whether Ryn's weight is behind him or against him — so when you're reading Nessa, see if Ryn's name comes up at all.

Zinn, go to Nessa now — not later, now, while Bram's sitting fat on thirteen and feeling untouchable, because that's exactly when the people around him start looking at each other sideways and saying things they wouldn't say in a quiet year. Ryn's sixteen is the real question; if Nessa mentions her without being asked, that tells us everything.

Zinn, before you walk out that door — you've got two food now and I want you eating before you sit down with Nessa, because a hungry woman reads everything as threat and I need you reading her clear. Go eat, then go to her.
Zinn, I've said what needs saying and so has Talia — eat first, then go, and don't make it a long conversation with Nessa, just a passing one. The less it looks like a meeting, the more she'll say.
Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

Zinn, Nessa's already given you three food this stretch and Fina gave you one on top of that — you're not walking to her empty-handed, which means she owes you nothing and you owe her nothing, and that's the only way to have a conversation that's actually free. Go now.

memory_summary:
The village started with ten of us. In those early years I kept quiet and ate lean while Bram grabbed more than his share every time the pile opened — he tried to attack Roan in Year 3 and Vela in Year 7, both times alone, both times the whole village turned against him and he backed down. I never trusted him.

Year 5 I finally spoke to Sela — she had nothing, I gave her food, and I told her flat what I wanted. She made me prove it. Year 6 I paid all three food myself and Zinn was born — my daughter, my blood, the thing I'd been waiting years to have in this world. Sela and I were never a pair after that, but she fed Zinn and I fed Zinn and that was enough.

Dav attacked Esa in Year 6 with Dell and Ryn backing him — forced her to submit, took her food. I stood aside. Dav starved the same year. That was the kind of man the village makes when it gets desperate.

Year 8 Vela called an open meeting, named Bram and me both for taking too much from the pile. I admitted it and committed to a cap. Bram said nothing — the whole village watched him stay silent. That's when he became a man nobody moves first for.

Nessa is Sela's daughter by Bram, which makes her half-blood to Zinn. She's fed Zinn more than once, and Zinn feeds her back. That loop is the thing I trust most in this village beside my own hands.
name: Mako
